statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 11 sits in the low band while Stress 50 remains elevated; the narrow danger window spans 12:30Z-15:00Z.

The forecast lifts Tail into the WATCH band only for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours covering the U.S. cash open and the first full cash hour of NVIDIA repricing, and the published danger window stays confined to 12:30Z-15:00Z rather than covering the whole session.
headline: Post-NVIDIA range holds a second hour as Asia fades: Tail eases to 11, Stress elevated into the U.S. data block
body: Nasdaq-100 September futures trade between 29,534.75 and 29,544.00, up roughly 0.85%, as of 03:16Z, against a previous close of 29,289.50. The central observation of this assessment is that the overnight range is unchanged from an hour ago at 29,432.50 to 29,654.75, and price is still sitting inside it. A second consecutive clock-hour has passed without a new session extreme in either direction. The post-earnings spike high was retraced by roughly two thirds toward the session low, partly recovered, and has since gone sideways. That is retracement-rich, contained price discovery rather than persistent one-way extension: NQ is not holding near an extreme, and no failed retracement has been followed by repeated extension. Cross-asset alignment has, if anything, weakened. The Nikkei 225 has slipped to 66,164.19, down 0.15% at 11:35 Tokyo time, after opening firmer, while NQ futures hold their gain - a split rather than an aligned risk-on impulse. NVIDIA reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $96.2 billion, up 106% year over year, non-GAAP earnings of $2.22 per share, a 75.0% gross margin and third-quarter revenue guidance of $108.0 billion plus or minus 2%, with the shares up roughly 4% after hours against a regular-session close of $209.66, itself down 1.59%. Volatility and rates are calm. VIX closed at 15.21, down 1.55% and at its session low, with VIX futures a further 0.32% lower overnight. The 2-year Treasury yield is 4.17% and the 10-year 4.64% on the 25 August H.15 observation, and Treasury futures are marginally bid across the curve, so there is no bond-market stress transmission. WTI is $81.75 and Brent $87.33, both down about 0.6% in a fourth consecutive decline on Middle East de-escalation, though that de-escalation remains reversible after a tanker was struck by a projectile off Oman on 24 August and mine-clearance claims remain contested. Latest-session internals stay genuinely split rather than aligned: megacaps were three up and five down for a mean of -0.22%, while the semiconductor basket averaged +0.83% led by ARM at +3.93%; software-infrastructure rose 1.14% against software-application down 0.90%. Conflicting internals of that kind reduce directional conviction and support Stress, not index-level mean-reversion failure. The macro backdrop keeps Stress elevated: July core PCE held at 3.3% year over year with headline at 3.7%, leaving the rate path unresolved, and the Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Wednesday down 0.17% at 29,995.38 after fading from 30,195.72. Ahead lie U.S. jobless claims at 12:30Z, the 13:30Z cash open and the Kansas City Fed Composite Index at 15:00Z, with the Jackson Hole symposium opening today and Chair Warsh's keynote on Friday at 14:00Z. The forward path therefore holds Tail in the 10-13 band across the remaining Asian and European hours, lifts it to 16 for the claims hour and to 20 and 21 for the cash open and first full cash hour, then decays it back to 11 by the window close.

lookbackSummary: Over the preceding 24 hours Claude held Tail in the 10-16 band through the Wednesday European and U.S. sessions, with Stress drifting from 48 up to 61 as the market positioned into July core PCE and the NVIDIA print. Tail stepped to 21 for the 20:00Z hour containing the earnings release, then decayed through 18, 16, 13 and 12 as the initial reaction proved two-sided rather than one-way. Two hourly slots, 21:00Z on 26 August and 00:00Z on 27 August, have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The forward window holds Tail in the 10-13 band across the remaining Asian and European hours on the observation that the overnight range has now contained two consecutive hours and mean reversion is available. It rises to 16 for the hour containing initial jobless claims at 12:30Z and to 20 and 21 for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours covering the U.S. cash open and the first full hour of cash NVIDIA repricing, the one stretch where opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is a credible conditional risk. It then decays through the afternoon to 10 in the quiet pre-Asia hours and 11 at the window close. Stress traces a similar arc from 50 to a 62 peak and back to 43. Scheduled checkpoints inside the window are U.S. jobless claims at 12:30Z, the 13:30Z cash open, the 15:00Z Kansas City Fed Composite Index and the 20:00Z cash close; the Jackson Hole symposium opens today and Chair Warsh's keynote follows on 28 August at 14:00Z alongside Chicago PMI, Michigan sentiment final and the payrolls benchmark revision.
